summary: Not ready. The tariff_code rule fails lint because its expression uses a `+` (BinOp) that the expression language doesn't allow. That one error makes 14 examples fail (all of AC-06.6.x and AC-06.7.3), including the main acceptance tests for the computed tariff code. A US-01.6 contradiction and a technical-vocabulary leak are also open. The other items are caveats: weak traceability on several items, two non-blocking open questions, and inconsistent 'asked' and 'required' wording.

findings.title: tariff_code rule does not evaluate (lint error); 14 examples fail
findings.why: The tariff code is the core output of the feature. The expression concatenates tariff_letter + child_count + church_tax_suffix with `+`, which the expression language rejects. No tariff code can be computed, and the 14 examples that expect one all fail.
findings.evidence: lint rule.tariff_code; examples AC-06.6.1 (7 cases), AC-06.6.2 (3), AC-06.6.3 (3), AC-06.7.3 'Employee answers no'. All show 'construct BinOp not allowed'.
findings.action: Rewrite the rule using the allowed constructs, e.g. a concat/format function, or one if_else branch per letter/digit/suffix. If concatenation is needed, add it to the expression language. Re-run the examples; there should be no expectation changes.

findings.title: The tariff rule does not implement the statement or table for the Liechtenstein >45 days and incomplete cases
findings.why: The statement says the more-than-45-days case carries a 'subject to the double taxation agreement' note and that an incomplete questionnaire gives 'incomplete - HR must complete' (D-048). The expression yields neither. Fixing the BinOp alone would still leave the rule short of its own spec.
findings.evidence: trace_judge rule.tariff_code; AC-06.6.3 'more than 45 non-return days' expects C0Y; AC-01.6.3 / D-048
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml how the DTA note and the incomplete result are represented (extra output field or text), and add both to the rule. Cite fb87f1 and cc19c7 in the rule.

findings.title: AC-01.6.2 contradicts AC-01.6.3
findings.why: After submission the questionnaire is read-only. The example nevertheless expects 'Denomination: asked' once HR records a change, while D-048 says the result becomes 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Engineering cannot tell whether the questionnaire reopens for the employee.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-01.6 (major); AC-01.6.1, AC-01.6.2, AC-01.6.3, D-048
findings.action: Decide whether HR completes the missing answer or the employee is asked again. Then fix the example, or AC-01.6.3, accordingly.

findings.title: Implementation vocabulary leaks into the spec
findings.why: D-045 forbids the word 'expression' in business text, and the 'ISO 3166' list name is implementation vocabulary. Engineering decisions should not be fixed in the spec.
findings.evidence: tech_leak feature.md and information.md ('The expression gives, per child…'); item.address_country, item.nationality, item.spouse_nationality, AC-02.3.1 ('ISO 3166')
findings.action: Reword the child-count note in business terms, e.g. 'the digit is the number of counted children'. Replace 'ISO 3166 country list' with 'list of countries'. Leave the standard to engineering.

findings.title: Facts cited by examples and conditions are not in the cited-fact lists
findings.why: Several story examples, items and rules rely on facts that are not in their cited sets. Most of these are the Maria and Tomás examples. This weakens traceability. Two claims are unbacked: Liechtenstein never gets the cross-border tariff, and Swiss nationals are exempt.
findings.evidence: trace_judge US-01.2, US-01.4, US-06.2, US-06.3, US-06.5, US-06.6, US-06.7, US-08.2 (AC-08.2.4), rule.cross_border_tariff, rule.questionnaire_flow, item.spouse_gainful_employment, item.has_children
findings.action: Add the missing source_refs (845204, b90bd9, 3f2c2a, cc19c7, d75286, 300c72, 97139a). Then confirm in decisions.yaml the Liechtenstein cross-border rule and the Swiss-national exemption, which no source states.

findings.title: Purpose claims and one rule row are unsupported or overstated
findings.why: Several purposes are stated as business rules without a source, and one rule row contradicts its source. Engineers will take them as confirmed.
findings.evidence: trace_judge item.child_main_financial_contributor ('H tariff'), item.non_return_days_60, item.daily_return_reasonable, item.first_working_day (age reference date), AC-03.1.4 ('HR plans the start'), US-06.2 (denomination not part of fund registration), rule.pension_fund_civil_status (partner date of birth also for Separated and Married, but D-003 covers registered partnership only)
findings.action: Either back each claim with a decision or source, or soften or remove it. For pension_fund_civil_status, confirm in decisions.yaml which civil statuses need the partner's date of birth.

findings.title: Inconsistent blocking behaviour and 'asked' versus 'required'
findings.why: The stories disagree on whether a missing required answer blocks the next step or only submission. The expected-result vocabulary also differs between stories, and '–' is undefined. Test cases will be ambiguous.
findings.action: Decide on one rule: block only submission, which fits the save-and-resume in US-01.7. Define 'asked' versus 'required' and the meaning of '–', then align the stories.

findings.title: Certificate-of-residence semantics are unclear
findings.why: The item is named 'handed in' and the calculator asks 'beigebracht', but the story asks whether the employee 'has' a certificate. This changes the meaning of yes/no/not yet, and what HR expects afterwards.
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml what 'yes', 'no' and 'not yet' mean, and when HR expects a certificate.

findings.title: Non-blocking open questions need owners before go-live
findings.why: The tariff code may differ from the Zurich calculator on unexplored paths. Several facts are only partly verified, and the pension portal form for Divorced and Widowed is unknown. The portal facts for the start date and canton are unused or unverified. The Germany questions for people living abroad are not specified.
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage, OQ-fund-divorced-widowed; fact_judge F-pension_portal-39bab1, -6d3630, -b359c3, -e45e5b; coverage F-pension_portal-3a97ab, F-hr_transcript-8595fb; US-03.1 date window
findings.action: Assign a domain expert to compare computed codes with the calculator before go-live. Ask the fund or HR to check the portal. Clarify how the insurance start date derives from the first working day, and what happens when the first working day is in the past.

findings.title: Inferred items remain unconfirmed
findings.why: Several rules and stories are inferred and rely on 'inferred, go-live check' examples. They also carry gaps such as Q14 being read as parental care, and Q16 being read as residence in Switzerland.
findings.evidence: inferred_items (spouse_nationality, church_tax_suffix, child_result, base_tariff_letter, US-05.2, US-07.3 to 07.5 and others); fact_judge F-zh_source_tax_calculator-64ac33, -037b1c, -dc0ae9, -2754e8
findings.action: Have HR or a domain expert confirm the inferred items and the calculator-question meanings, and record them in decisions.yaml.
